standards.title: Tire Size Standards
standards.description: Bicycle tires use various sizing standards. Understanding the difference between ETRTO, inch, and French notations is key to finding the right fit.

etrto.name: ETRTO (ISO)
etrto.description: The modern European standard. It indicates width and inner diameter, making it the most unambiguous and recommended method.

inch.name: Inch (Imperial)
inch.description: Traditional notation. It indicates approximate outer diameter and width, but can be imprecise because one inch label may refer to different diameters.

french.name: French
french.description: This notation indicates approximate outer diameter and width. The letter C hints at the inner diameter and is common on road and gravel tires.

mystery.title: The "28 Inch" vs "29 Inch" Mystery
mystery.sameDescription: Both 28 inch touring or road tires and 29 inch MTB tires fit on the same 622 mm rim diameter.
mystery.contextBody: 28 inches is the traditional European size for touring bikes. 29 inches is a marketing term introduced in the US for voluminous MTB tires that have an approximate outer diameter of 29 inches when mounted.
mystery.realityBody: Both designations are imprecise. A narrow 28 inch road tire can be about 26 inches in outer diameter, while a wide 60 mm or larger MTB tire can be almost 30 inches.
